To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The health and well-being of people experiencing homelessness is affected by their social and economic conditions and the way in which they are treated by society and the health system.
Homelessness is a social determinant of health.
The health of homeless people is poor, and their health needs are complex and often not well met.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which homelessness and health are linked.
the ways in which social determinants of homelessness impact on health, and the ways in which homelessness impacts on social determinants of population health.
how the social determinants and conditions of homelessness shape health and wellbeing, and how health and wellbeing in turn influence homelessness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
homelessness and its consequences have an enormous negative impact on health.
homelessness is a major public health issue in Australia.
people experiencing homelessness have poorer health outcomes and are at increased risk for a wide range of negative health outcomes than the general population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to provide a more holistic and comprehensive picture of homelessness and its impact on the health and wellbeing of individuals and communities.
homelessness and health are linked in complex ways and that homelessness is a health problem.
the social determinants are the key to improving health and wellbeing outcomes for people experiencing homelessness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
homelessness and health are inextricably linked and that the social determinants approach can be used to reframe the links between the two.
the links between homelessness, health and well-being can be understood through a social determinants of heath lens.
homelessness is not just an individual problem.
